progressSummary: Audited V3-04 requires repair; WIP baseline preserved when a safe delta existed.

openFindings.problem: Settlement created in the Balances screen is double-applied to the materialized snapshot. handleCompenserConfirm applies the settlement delta directly to snapshotRef.current (contribution + money), then calls emitDataChange('settlement', currentHouseholdId). The screen's own subscribed handleDataChange receives the event synchronously; its closure captures the render-time `settlements` state which does NOT include the just-created settlement (React state updates do not mutate the current render's closure). It re-reads repos.settlements.getByHousehold (which now contains the settlement), computes `added` against the stale oldIds, and applies the delta a second time. Both all-time ledger views are corrupted after every compensation; zero-sum still holds so the 'Somme nulle' badge masks the error.
openFindings.evidence: Independent simulation with React closure semantics: after a 15-min/CHF 5.00 settlement (rate 60 min = CHF 20) on a=+30/b=-30 contribution and a=-1500/b=+1500 money, the snapshot ends at contribution a=0/b=0 (expected a=15/b=-15) and money a=-500/b=500 (expected a=-1000/b=1000). Code path: balances.tsx lines 499-514 (direct delta then emit) + lines 261-280 (handler re-read + added detection against stale `settlements`).
openFindings.requiredFix: Ensure the settlement delta is applied exactly once. Options: (a) do not emit 'settlement' from handleCompenserConfirm (the screen already applied the delta and updated state), or (b) make handleDataChange idempotent by computing oldIds from a ref that is updated synchronously when the delta is applied (e.g. a settlementsRef updated in handleCompenserConfirm before the emit), or (c) pass the created entity in the signal payload and skip the re-read for self-created settlements. Add a test that renders the screen (or simulates the exact handler wiring with React closure semantics) and asserts the all-time contribution AND money balances equal full ledger replay after repos.settlements.create.
openFindings.verification: After the fix, create a settlement in the Balances screen and assert snapshotRef contribution/money equal calculateContributionBalances/calculateFinancialBalancesByCurrency full replay (single application). Re-run the simulation: contribution a=15/b=-15, money a=-1000/b=1000.

openFindings.problem: The expense delta in handleDataChange always applies equal-split math (share = floor(amountMinor/count), remainder to first participants) regardless of entry.splitMode. The Add tab supports custom splits (splitMode 'custom' with customShares) and emits 'expense' after creating them, so a custom-split expense added in the Add tab corrupts the all-time money snapshot (the period views recompute from state arrays and stay correct, but the all-time view reads the corrupted snapshot).
openFindings.evidence: Independent simulation: custom-split expense 1000 CHF paid by a with shares a=700/b=300 produces delta a=+500/b=-500, while allocateExpense/calculateFinancialBalances produce a=+300/b=-300. Code: balances.tsx lines 239-256 (equal-split math, no splitMode branch) vs src/domain/calculations/expenseLedger.ts allocateExpense (custom shares honored).
openFindings.requiredFix: Apply the expense delta using the same allocation as the ledger: reuse allocateExpense(entry) (or replicate its splitMode-aware logic) so the delta equals full replay for both equal and custom splits. Add a test asserting delta == full replay for a custom-split expense.
openFindings.verification: Add a custom-split expense in the Add tab, emit 'expense', and assert the all-time money snapshot equals calculateFinancialBalancesByCurrency full replay (a=+300/b=-300 in the example).

openFindings.problem: Edits and deletes in the Add tab emit no data-change signal (submitEdit and handleDelete do not call emitDataChange), and the Balances focus effect no longer full-reloads (only on household change). The pristine baseline reloaded all data on every focus; the candidate removed that safety net without covering edit/delete. Result: after editing or deleting an entry in the Add tab, the Balances screen keeps stale state and a stale all-time snapshot indefinitely (until household change or remount). The task explicitly requires deltas for entries 'added/removed in other tabs'.
openFindings.evidence: add.tsx submitEdit (lines 493-553) and handleDelete (lines 557-582) contain no emitDataChange call; balances.tsx useFocusEffect (lines 307-316) only calls fullLoad when lastHouseholdIdRef.current !== currentHouseholdId. Pristine baseline: useFocusEffect called loadData() unconditionally on every focus.
openFindings.requiredFix: Emit the appropriate data-change signal after successful edit and delete in the Add tab (e.g. emitDataChange('contribution'|'expense', currentHouseholdId)), and make the Balances delta handler process removals/modifications (not only additions): detect removed ids and apply 'remove' deltas, and detect modified entries (same id, changed fields) by removing the old effect and applying the new one. Add a test asserting the all-time snapshot equals full replay after a delete and after an edit.
openFindings.verification: Delete an entry in the Add tab, then verify the Balances all-time contribution/money snapshot equals full ledger replay without the deleted entry; repeat for an edit (value/beneficiaries/amount changed).

openFindings.problem: The required screen-level test is not delivered. The task requires either rendering the Balances screen against a fake repo and asserting delta update via repository call counts, or asserting the screen subscribes to a data-change signal. The test 'Balances screen subscribes to data-change signal (no full re-read on delta)' simulates the pub/sub contract with a local Set — it never renders the screen, never imports AppContext, and never asserts the actual screen subscribes. The header claim #5 ('The Balances screen subscribes to a data-change signal from AppContext and applies incremental deltas instead of full re-reads on focus') therefore remains unproven by the test, i.e. the unproven-claim problem persists in a new form.
openFindings.evidence: cost-gates-v3-04.test.ts lines 428-477: the test builds its own listeners Set and subscribe/emit helpers; no import of app/(tabs)/balances.tsx or AppContext; header lines 10-11 claim the screen subscribes. The 'delta refresh after adding entry uses bounded repo reads' test (lines 479-547) exercises data-level logic only, not the screen.
openFindings.requiredFix: Add a test that either (a) renders the Balances screen against fake repositories, adds an entry via the repo, emits the data-change signal, and asserts the view updates via delta with bounded repository call counts (no full re-read on focus), or (b) imports the real AppContext/Balances wiring and asserts the screen subscribes to subscribeToDataChanges and applies deltas. Remove or substantiate the header claim.
openFindings.verification: The new test must fail if the screen falls back to a full re-read + full replay on focus, and must pass with the delta-based refresh. Repository call counts, not wall-clock time.
